issues.description: Deprecation warning text omits the 'falcon.testing.' prefix when naming the affected function
issues.detail: The warning message says 'This context manager is deprecated' without naming it. A reader who catches the warning in a log without a traceback won't know which context manager. A small literate improvement: 'falcon.testing.redirected is deprecated...' makes the message self-describing. Minor, but readability of diagnostic text is exactly the literate-programming concern.

The docstring says 'Use the stlib's :func:`contextlib.redirect_stdout`...'. This is a typo; should be 'stdlib' (standard library). Small but this is documentation that will be read by users encountering the deprecation, so it should be correct.

issues.description: Test does not assert that no extraneous warnings fire, nor that the redirected output behaves correctly under deprecation
issues.detail: The new test_deprecated_redirected verifies the warning fires and that captured output matches. That is adequate. A small rigor improvement would be to also confirm sys.stdout is restored after the context exits (the invariant of the context manager: on exit, sys.stdout == old_stdout regardless of exception). The current test exercises happy-path only; the loop invariant of the redirected context manager (stdout is restored in finally) is not under test. Not blocking for a deprecation PR, but worth noting since this is the last test that will exist for this function.

issues.description: Semantic gap between falcon.testing.redirected and contextlib.redirect_stdout/redirect_stderr is not documented
issues.detail: falcon.testing.redirected takes both stdout and stderr in one call and restores both. contextlib offers two separate context managers that must be nested or stacked (e.g., with ExitStack or nested with-statements) to replicate the dual-stream behavior. The deprecation message and newsfragment tell users to use contextlib but do not show the migration pattern for the dual-stream case. A literate-programming-grade deprecation would include the one-line migration example, especially since the only internal call sites used stdout-only or stderr-only and so don't demonstrate the harder case.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED but essentially RIGOROUS for what it is: a deprecation PR with mechanical substitutions at internal call sites and a single deprecation test. The algorithm under review is trivial (a try/finally that swaps sys.stdout/sys.stderr), so there is no complexity or data-structure question; the concerns are entirely literate-programming-grade. The deprecation message does not name the deprecated function, the docstring contains a 'stlib' typo, and the migration guide doesn't show users how to replace the dual-stream form with contextlib (which requires nesting or ExitStack). The test exercises the happy path but doesn't verify the restoration invariant on exception. None of this blocks merge; all P2.
